# A limit must be an integer expression that is the same on every evaluation and
# cannot panic. A field, a call, a division by a variable, a limit the body
# assigns, zero, a non-int limit, and a <= limit that could overflow when one is
# added are left alone.

cp ops.go ops.go.orig
loopvec -split .
! stdout .
! stderr .
! exists ops_simd.go
cmp ops.go ops.go.orig

-- go.mod --
module example.com/test

go 1.27.1
-- ops.go --
package test

type T struct{ n int }

func Field(t T, x, y []float32) {
	for i := 0; i < t.n; i++ {
		y[i] += x[i]
	}
}

func Zero(x, y []float32) {
	for i := 0; i < 0; i++ {
		y[i] += x[i]
	}
}

func Narrow(n int32, x, y []float32) {
	for i := range n {
		y[i] += x[i]
	}
}

func LessOrEqual(n int, x, y []float32) {
	for i := 0; i <= n; i++ {
		y[i] += x[i]
	}
}

func Call(n int, x, y []float32) {
	for i := 0; i < abs(n); i++ {
		y[i] += x[i]
	}
}

func abs(n int) int { return max(n, -n) }

func DivideByVariable(n, m int, x, y []float32) {
	for i := 0; i < n/m; i++ {
		y[i] += x[i]
	}
}

func LimitAssigned(n int, x, y []float32) {
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		y[i] += x[i]
		n = n - 1
	}
}
